use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

evidence_cards.content: The protocols in this section are to be followed in order to minimize occurrences and duration of dual designations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the objective (goal) of the protocols described in the document, which is to reduce how often dual designations happen and how long they last.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to determine if two tracks shall be correlated based on passing specific correlation tests and restrictions, such that they are processed for dual designation resolution.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the high-level goal of the use case: resolving dual designations through the process of track correlation as specified by the C2 JU requirements.

evidence_cards.content: Track correlation prevents/eliminates dual designations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the high-level objective of the process described in the use case, which is to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: The goal of the use case is to resolve dual designations that occur when two tracks represent the same object.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement explicitly defines the high-level objective (resolving dual designations) that the primary actor aims to achieve in this context.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.4.3.1 (AIR AND SURFACE TRACK CORRELATION), second paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the mandatory system capability required before the use case can proceed to compare locally derived sensor data with interface data.

evidence_cards.content: Positions of all tracks and IUs tested for correlation shall be extrapolated to the same time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a mandatory system state that must hold before the correlation test can occur; it defines a precondition on track data alignment required for the use case to proceed.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This imposes a temporal constraint on when the correlation test may begin relative to the extrapolated state — a critical timing precondition for initiating the use case.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates that the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific system state regarding ID conflicts that must be evaluated as a precondition before automatic correlation can occur.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific system state regarding Mode II code discrepancies that acts as a restriction on the use case.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a condition where tracks are both local, preventing correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a threshold condition for the Strength field that prevents correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if one track is a common local track and the other is a remote, and the same unit has R² for both tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific tracking configuration involving common local and remote tracks that inhibits correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if either track is currently the subject of a dual designation resolution action involving another TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Indicates that ongoing resolution actions on other tracks serve as a blocking condition.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if each track is subject to one or more operational contingency constraints (OCC), such as being the subject of a current engagement status message, a pending command message, a controlled track, or an active/inactive IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Lists specific operational states (OCCs) that must not exist for the tracks to be correlated.

evidence_cards.content: A C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the system state where the primary actor has identified a dual designation candidate, serving as the necessary condition before initiating the resolution process.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs capable of reporting air or surface tracks shall have the capability to transmit and receive all the response values of the J7.2 message for real-time air and/or surface tracks, which are held locally by their system.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms the required system capability (local holding of tracks and J7.2 messaging support) must exist for the use case to proceed.

evidence_cards.content: The C² JU initiates a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number after the PPLI and local track data are decorrelated due to meeting a system's decorrelation criteria.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the triggering event for initiating a new track (and thus resolving dual designation via correlation failure/decorrelation), which is an alternative path in the use case where correlation tests fail and decorrelation occurs.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall perform correlation tests in response to correlation requests from other units.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly identifies the 'correlation request from other units' as the event that triggers the C2 JU's action (performing correlation tests), which is the core of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks are tested again upon the next correlation stimulus after a tentative correlation is established.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event (next correlation stimulus) that triggers the second test leading to dual designation resolution processing.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the event (recognition of eligible tracks) and the immediate actor response (initiate action) that constitutes the trigger for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: A C2 JU participating on the Surveillance Network PG shall attempt to correlate received PPLI reports with data being received from local sensors.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the primary action in the main flow where the actor initiates correlation testing between incoming reports and existing tracks.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which the C2 JU has R2, the J7.2 Correlation message shall be transmitted with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), and with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This details the specific system response and data handling when a correlation is successfully identified and the local unit retains responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the final step in the successful resolution sequence where the redundant track is dropped.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall make an automatic correlation test either: (a) Upon receipt of each remote real-time J3.2 or J3.3 track or J2.0 (Originator E/C = 0 or 3), J2.2, or J2.3 PPLI report which is not confirmed to have an existing correlation to a local track; OR (b) Immediately prior to each transmission of a local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific trigger events and timing for the automatic correlation process in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: Such tests shall compare the received remote track or IU to local tracks of the same E/C, including previously common local tracks for which own unit has R².
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the comparison criteria required during the automatic correlation test step.

evidence_cards.content: Correlation testing shall consist of the position, velocity, and altitude tests specified in this paragraph.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the mandatory set of tests that must be performed to resolve dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: Positions of all tracks and IUs tested for correlation shall be extrapolated to the same time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the data preparation step required before the actual comparison can occur.

evidence_cards.content: A local track shall be considered to correlate to the closest remote track or IU that meets all of the correlation tests, subject to the correlation restrictions in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g and the requirement to pass two correlation tests in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1h.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the success condition for the correlation process and the resolution of the dual designation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks; or (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific restrictions that prevent the automatic correlation step in the main flow when certain data conflicts exist between tracks.

evidence_cards.content: When the remote report being tested for correlation is a J2.0 Indirect PPLI message with the Originator E/C field set to value 0 (Surface) or 3 (Air), it shall be processed for correlation like a J3.2 air or J3.3 surface (maritime) track with TQ = 7.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a processing rule within the correlation test sequence for specific message types, detailing how they are treated during the evaluation.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall pass the correlation tests and restrictions in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and 4.4.4.3.1g 2(1-2,1) times before the correlation is executed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the initial step in the main flow: repeated testing requirement before correlation can proceed.

evidence_cards.content: When two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they shall be deemed a tentative correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an intermediate state in the main flow after first successful test pass.

evidence_cards.content: The same two tracks shall be tested again upon the next correlation stimulus (see paragraph 4.4.4.3.1c).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the second required test event in the main flow sequence.

evidence_cards.content: If the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they shall be processed for dual designation resolution in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1j and k.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the final step in the main flow: successful completion leads to dual designation resolution processing.

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the initiating action in the main flow sequence where the actor requests resolution from the system/network.

evidence_cards.content: The message identifies the TN (Track Number) to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the critical data payload required in the main flow request to define the resolution outcome.

evidence_cards.content: The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the standard system response (acceptance) in the main flow, establishing the default success path before exceptions.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU receives or generates a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 (Correlation Acceptance), it shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of three restrictions applies: (1) tracks are of different E/C or have existing E/C conflict; (2) one track is simulated and the other is live; or (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks — in which case the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the canonical success path for automatic correlation acceptance under RV=3, including explicit rejection conditions that represent exceptions to the main flow — directly constraining the step-by-step interaction sequence between actor and system during normal operation.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be subject to automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a post-acceptance constraint that affects subsequent system behavior following successful correlation — relevant as an observable state change immediately after completion of the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which the C2 JU has R², the J7.2 Correlation message shall be transmitted with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), and with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary success path where the C2 JU accepts the incoming PPLI report (Retained TN) and drops its own local surveillance track (Dropped TN) upon finding a match.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the specific system action required to terminate the redundant local track after correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall make an automatic correlation test either upon receipt of each remote real-time track or PPLI report which is not confirmed to have an existing correlation to a local track, or immediately prior to each transmission of a local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific triggers for the system to initiate the main flow of automatic correlation testing.

evidence_cards.content: Correlation tests shall include active IUs, remote real-time tracks, and other local tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the scope of data entities involved in the correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: Positions of all tracks and IUs tested for correlation shall be extrapolated to the same time. The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the mandatory temporal alignment procedure required before comparing tracks.

evidence_cards.content: A local track shall be considered to correlate to the closest remote track or IU that meets all of the correlation tests.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the success criteria for identifying the matching track among candidates.

evidence_cards.content: Correlation testing shall consist of the position, velocity, and altitude tests specified in this paragraph.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific types of tests performed during the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines mandatory restrictions that prevent automatic correlation during the main flow of resolving dual designations via track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The restrictions do not apply to manual correlation. No other correlation restrictions shall be applied for two tracks which pass the correlation tests specified in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies that manual correlation bypasses these restrictions and that no additional restrictions beyond those listed apply if tests are passed — critical for defining the canonical success scenario boundaries.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit this automatic restriction [for ID conflict or Mode II code mismatch], subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C² IUs; if use changes, all participating C² IUs will be informed through voice communication or other media; in lieu of specific direction, all IUs will restrict automatic correlation by default.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies configurable exceptions to the automatic correlation restrictions, allowing operators to override them under coordinated conditions — part of the normal interaction sequence when such overrides are invoked.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall pass the correlation tests and restrictions in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and 4.4.4.3.1g 2(1-2,1) times before the correlation is executed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific testing frequency required for two tracks to be considered eligible for tentative correlation, which is a key step in the main flow of resolving dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: When two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they shall be deemed a tentative correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the intermediate state ('tentative correlation') achieved after the first successful pass of tests, marking progress in the main flow sequence.

evidence_cards.content: The same two tracks shall be tested again upon the next correlation stimulus (see paragraph 4.4.4.3.1c).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the re-testing requirement that follows a tentative correlation, continuing the sequence towards final resolution.

evidence_cards.content: If the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they shall be processed for dual designation resolution in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1j and k.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the final success condition where passing the second test leads directly to processing for dual designation resolution, completing the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the primary actor's initial action in the main flow upon recognizing eligible tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system interaction step where the originating unit requests correlation from others.

evidence_cards.content: The message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the content payload required in the correlation request message.

evidence_cards.content: The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the default acceptance behavior for receiving units in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If no tentative correlation is found on the initial test, the new local track shall be transmitted immediately rather than being held for further testing.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where the track is reported immediately upon failing the first correlation test, diverging from the main flow's requirement to pass two tests.

evidence_cards.content: If the new local track tentatively correlates on the initial test but fails correlation on the next test, the new local track shall be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where a tentative correlation is rejected after the second test, resulting in immediate transmission instead of dual designation resolution.

evidence_cards.content: A manual capability shall be provided to initiate the correlation of any two tracks irrespective of the standard correlation test criteria, restrictions, or requirements, except that tracks cannot be manually correlated if they are of different E/C, one is simulated and the other live, or both are remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a manual alternative flow for initiating correlation that bypasses the automatic test criteria and restrictions defined in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the operator shall be alerted to take one of the following actions: (a) Change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation, or (b) Transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a successful alternative flow where the standard automatic correlation path diverges due to conflicting IDs, but resolution is achieved through specific operator interventions rather than system rejection.

evidence_cards.content: JUs may apply one exception to the restriction regarding identity conflicts and operational contingency constraints (OCC). If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a specific legal alternative path that overrides standard restrictions (identity conflict and OCC), allowing the process to proceed successfully under defined engagement conditions.

evidence_cards.content: If the Identity of Retained TN and Dropped TN are different and the difference would result in automatic acceptance of the Dropped TN ID/IAD in accordance with Table 4.7-2, the Dropped TN ID/IAD and Special Interest Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type shall be transferred to Retained TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative data transfer path during correlation when identity restrictions are not inhibited and specific criteria are met.

evidence_cards.content: When the Identity of Retained TN and Dropped TN are different, the last Identity reported for Dropped TN shall be considered equivalent to a J7.0 (ACT = 1) Identity Difference Report for the Retained TN. It shall be processed in accordance with paragraph 4.7.1.2.2 immediately after the correlation is executed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where a correlation results in the generation and processing of an Identity Difference Report rather than immediate full data transfer.

evidence_cards.content: If the local track satisfies decorrelation criteria but fails the subsequent automatic correlation test against remote tracks, a new TN (TN B) shall be assigned to the local track and reported in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative outcome where a track is decorrelated and re-assigned a new identifier instead of maintaining the original correlation.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 (manually initiated), it shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless specific restrictions apply: (1) the two tracks are of a different E/C or have an existing E/C conflict; (2) one track is simulated and the other is live; or (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a successful alternative flow where a manually initiated correlation request is accepted despite being outside the standard automatic process, provided no hard restrictions exist.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held by the receiving C2 JU, the system processes the request differently based on the RV field: if RV is 0, transmit reverse correlation with RV=1; if RV is 1, transmit rejection with RV=2; if RV is 3, execute correlation using Dropped TN data and Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a valid alternative path for resolving dual designations when the receiving unit does not hold the originally proposed 'Retained' track but holds the 'Dropped' one, allowing for role reversal or execution based on manual initiation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs responding with a reverse correlation shall transmit the J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the successful alternative action of reversing the correlation proposal (swapping Retained/Dropped roles) when the original proposal is unacceptable but correlation is still desired.

evidence_cards.content: If no tentative correlation is found on the initial test, the new local track shall be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception path where the standard requirement to wait for a second test (or successful correlation) is bypassed due to immediate failure of the first test.

evidence_cards.content: If the new local track tentatively correlates on the initial test but fails correlation on the next test, the new local track shall be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception path where a tentative correlation is rejected after failing the mandatory second verification test, resulting in transmission rather than merging.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) Identity (ID) difference constituting a conflict; (2) different Mode II codes with current local Mode II code; (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks being updated with local positional data; or (4) either track has Strength field set to value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific exception conditions that prevent automatic correlation — these are terminal blocking states for the main flow unless overridden by operator action or interface coordination

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit the automatic restriction for ID conflicts or Mode II code mismatches, subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C² IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides recovery mechanism for exceptions — allows manual override of automatic correlation restrictions under controlled conditions

evidence_cards.content: In lieu of specific interface direction, all IUs will restrict automatic correlation by default when using the override capability for ID or Mode II restrictions.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies safe default behavior after exception handling — ensures conservative correlation policy unless explicitly coordinated

evidence_cards.content: If the use of the override capability changes, all participating C² IUs will be informed through voice communication or other communications media.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Mandates notification protocol for exception handling state changes — ensures consistency across distributed units during exception resolution

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall not inhibit correlation if either track has Strength set to No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies boundary condition for Strength-based exception — prevents false positive inhibition when strength is unspecified

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 0 or 1, it shall not accept the requested correlation if local or remote data indicates: (1) a correlation restriction exists (e.g., identity conflict), (2) the tracks would decorrelate upon testing, (3) there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and received RV is 0, or (4) there is an OCC on the Dropped TN and received RV is 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific conditions under which an automatic correlation request is rejected by the receiving unit.

evidence_cards.content: If a C2 JU rejects a correlation request due to restrictions, it must transmit a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the system response (message transmission) required when a correlation exception occurs.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected (RV=2), the originating JU shall not automatically originate another request with the same Retained/Dropped TN pair for a period of 2 minutes (range 1-10,1).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a retry constraint/throttle following a rejection exception.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 3 (manual correlation) shall automatically accept unless: (1) tracks are different E/C or have existing E/C conflict, (2) one track is simulated and the other live, or (3) both are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies exceptions where even a manually initiated correlation request must be rejected.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held, and the Dropped TN has an OCC: if RV is 0, transmit reverse correlation with RV=1; if RV is 1, transmit correlation rejection with RV=2.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes exception handling logic based on track ownership (Retained vs Dropped) and OCC status.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.2 Correlation message shall not be inhibited by any filter.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes that even when transmission filters are active (which would normally inhibit track reporting), the critical correlation resolution message is exempted from filtering — ensuring the exception path for dual designation resolution remains unblocked.

evidence_cards.content: Targets reported in J12.7 messages shall be processed as EW Product information for the purposes of environment/category filtering.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception handling rule: EW-targets (J12.7) are treated differently under filtering rules, which may affect whether they are eligible for correlation or how they interact with filter-based inhibition — relevant to exception flows involving electronic warfare tracks.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This claim describes an exception handling path where the local unit does not hold the authority (R²) to resolve the dual designation; instead of accepting the correlation locally, it must transmit a specific reverse correlation message to the unit that holds authority.

evidence_cards.content: Subsurface tracks shall not be correlated with IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This claim defines a hard restriction/exception condition where correlation is explicitly prohibited based on track type (subsurface vs. IU), preventing the standard resolution flow from occurring.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates that the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception condition (Identity Conflict) that prevents the automatic correlation flow from proceeding.

evidence_cards.content: If an Identity (ID) conflict exists, systems must restrict automatic correlation by default unless interface coordination has promulgated a change to allow it; this capability requires operator selection and communication to all participating C2 IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the handling path for the ID conflict exception: default restriction with a manual override mechanism requiring coordination.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception condition (Mode II Code Mismatch) that prevents the automatic correlation flow from proceeding.

evidence_cards.content: If a Mode II code mismatch exists, systems must restrict automatic correlation by default unless interface coordination has promulgated a change to allow it; this capability requires operator selection and communication to all participating C2 IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the handling path for the Mode II mismatch exception: default restriction with a manual override mechanism requiring coordination.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks (i.e., being updated with local positional data).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception condition (Dual Local Real-Time Tracks) that prevents the automatic correlation flow from proceeding.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception condition (Strength Field > 1) that prevents the automatic correlation flow from proceeding.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation shall be deemed to have failed if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received for the dropped TN after a period of 60 seconds from the transmission of the correlation request and all associated processing for the correlation shall be cancelled.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception condition (timeout) where the correlation process fails and must be cancelled.

evidence_cards.content: If the Dropped TN is reported by another IU after transmission of the J7.0, own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt to correlate the Retained TN and the Dropped TN for a period of 60 seconds after transmission of the J7.0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception scenario where the dropped track reappears, triggering a mandatory 60-second suspension of re-correlation attempts.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R² for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after transmitting the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific exception handling path where the originator possesses ownership rights (R²) for the track designated to be dropped, requiring an additional cleanup message transmission.

evidence_cards.content: Transmission of a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 0 or 1 shall be discontinued upon receipt of a J7.2 message containing one or both of the same TNs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an interruption condition for the main flow correlation request process triggered by conflicting incoming messages.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Lists specific terminal exception conditions that force rejection of a manually initiated correlation request despite the high-priority RV=3 setting.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a post-exception constraint preventing immediate automatic reversal of a manually resolved dual designation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs rejecting a J7.2 message and holding the Dropped TN as a local or common local track shall not interpret the J7.2 message as a Drop Track message for the purpose of determining R².
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies exception behavior regarding data retention and status determination when a correlation request is rejected.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R² and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception handling path where a correlation request results in a rejection response (RV=1) rather than acceptance due to ownership conflicts.

evidence_cards.content: Subsurface tracks shall not be correlated with IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific restriction/exception condition that prevents the correlation process from occurring between these entity types.

evidence_cards.content: If an operator action has been taken which selectively released a new local track for reporting, it shall be transmitted, regardless of the results of correlation testing.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an exception to the standard correlation test requirement: operator override forces transmission even if correlation tests fail or are pending, constituting an error/unexpected condition handling path where normal rules are bypassed.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU receiving a J7.2 Correlation message and also holding OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks (if the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled) shall reject the correlation in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.2a(1).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific rejection condition for the exception flow when a correlation request conflicts with existing Operational Contingency Constraints or identity conflicts.

evidence_cards.content: The Unknown/Hostile track shall be the dropped Track Number (TN-2) if automatic correlation is allowed under the engagement exception; this exception allows breaking the engagement and/or destroying missile(s) in flight.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the resolution logic (dropping the hostile track) as part of the exception handling for engagement status conflicts.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 0 or 1 shall not accept the requested correlation when local or remote data held indicates one or more of the following conditions exist: (1) There is a correlation restriction as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g; (2) The Retained TN and the Dropped TN will decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once; (3) There is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 0; (4) There is an OCC on the Dropped TN and the received RV field is set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific exception conditions where a receiving C2 JU must reject a correlation request based on restrictions, decorrelation potential, or OCC constraints combined with RV values.

evidence_cards.content: Whenever a correlation request is rejected the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the system response (transmission of J7.2 with RV=2) required when a correlation request is rejected.

evidence_cards.content: If a selection conflict occurs due to OCCs on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception handling path where correlation is abandoned rather than executed due to conflicting OCCs on both tracks.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies, in which case the correlation shall be rejected: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies exceptions that override the automatic acceptance rule for manually initiated correlations (RV=3), forcing rejection instead.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs rejecting the requested correlation shall initiate transmission of a J7.2 message with the Retained TN/Dropped TN set as received and RV field set to value 2.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Confirms the mandatory response format for any C2 JU that rejects a correlation request.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU ceases reporting the track and transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message on the surveillance TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system action that terminates the dual designation reporting for the dropped track upon successful correlation resolution.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.2 Correlation message is transmitted with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the final state of the correlation request as non-negotiable when the local unit holds R-squared authority.

evidence_cards.content: The Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message is retained as the Retained TN, and the surveillance TN is designated as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the resulting track identity assignments after the use case resolves the dual designation.

evidence_cards.content: If own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN shall be designated as a common local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific state designation of the Retained Track Number immediately following a successful correlation where the dropped track was local/common.

evidence_cards.content: If own unit has R² for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message shall be transmitted for the Dropped TN, and own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the state of the Dropped Track Number (retained as remote) and the action taken (transmission of drop message) when the unit had responsibility (R²) for it.

evidence_cards.content: When a J7.2 message is initiated by own unit and a Drop Track message has not yet been received for the Dropped TN, it shall be retained as a remote track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the interim state of the Dropped TN during the correlation execution process before final confirmation.

evidence_cards.content: Kinematic Data (Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, Altitude Source, TQ, and Strength) from the Dropped TN shall be transferred to the Retained TN if the Dropped TN is a local or common local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the data state change of the Retained TN, incorporating specific kinematic attributes from the Dropped TN upon successful correlation.

evidence_cards.content: If the Identity (ID) or Identity Amplifying Descriptor (IAD) of two exercise tracks are different and the difference results in automatic acceptance, the Dropped TN ID/IAD, Special Interest Indicator, Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type shall be transferred to the Retained TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the identification data state of the Retained TN when merging tracks with different IDs that are automatically accepted.

evidence_cards.content: When the Identity of Retained TN and Dropped TN are the same, associated identification data (Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, Exercise Indicator, and Special Interest Indicator) reported for the Retained TN shall be retained.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the identification data state of the Retained TN when merging tracks with identical IDs.

evidence_cards.content: Any Dropped TN nonzero Mode I, II, or III IFF/SIF data for a mode for which the Retained TN data is zero shall be transferred to the Retained TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific condition under which IFF/SIF data is merged into the Retained TN's state.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV=3), the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific post-use-case state constraint regarding system behavior (automatic decorrelation) following successful manual correlation.

evidence_cards.content: If the originating C2 JU holds R² for the Dropped TN, it shall drop the Dropped TN and transmit the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message after the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific system action (dropping a track and transmitting a termination message) that occurs upon successful resolution when specific authority conditions are met.
